narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 75% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is a probability, not a certainty, but it was high enough to drive the rejection decision.

The strongest factor was your third-year class standing. You were in the second decile, far below the average of about the sixth decile among accepted students, and this pushed the prediction toward bar-exam failure. Your first-year standing was the next most influential factor. You were in the third decile, compared with an accepted-student average of about six, and this also pushed toward failure. Your LSAT score had a smaller influence, and it worked in your favor: a score of 38 was slightly above the accepted-student average of about 37.18, pushing toward passing. However, it was not enough to outweigh the concerns raised by your class standing.

To strengthen a future application, ask admissions for specific feedback and meet with an academic advisor. Focus on raising your academic performance in advanced law coursework, seek support for bar-exam-style analytical writing and study planning, and document any meaningful improvement before reapplying. You may also consider schools or conditional-admission programs that assess applicants more holistically.
